record.title: The square-value conjecture for partition functions $P_n$
record.statement:
Let $n\in\mathbb{N}_{\geq 6}$, and let $P_n$ be the partition function associated with the set of parts $\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$. Consider positive integer solutions $(x,y)$ of

$$
y^2=P_n(x).
$$

**Square-value conjecture for $P_n$.** The only positive integer solution is

$$
x=y=1.
$$

The paper discusses computations for the cases $n=6$ and related hyperelliptic curves, but the asserted statement for every $n\geq 6$ remains open.
record.source_name: Szabolcs Tengely and Maciej Ulas, “Equal values of certain partition functions via Diophantine equations”, arXiv:2102.05352 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.05352

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2021).

record.title: Equidistribution of d-th power partitions modulo every integer
record.statement:
Let $d\in\mathbb{N}_{\geq 2}$ be fixed, and define the $d$-th power partition function $p_d(n)$ by

$$
\prod_{k=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{1-q^{k^d}}=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}p_d(n)q^n.
$$

**Equidistribution conjecture.** For every $m\in\mathbb{N}_{\geq 2}$ and every $r\in\\{0,\ldots,m-1\\}$, there are infinitely many $n\in\mathbb{N}$ such that

$$
p_d(n)\equiv r\pmod{m}.
$$

This conjecture predicts that every residue class modulo every integer occurs infinitely often among the values of $p_d(n)$. The source reports computational data for small values of $d$ and $n$, but gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Maciej Ulas, “Some observations and speculations on partitions into d-th powers”, arXiv:2102.05355 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.05355

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2021).

record.title: Asymptotic strengthened log-concavity conjecture for d-th power partitions
record.statement:
Let $d\in\mathbb{N}_{\geq 2}$, and let $p_d(n)$ denote the number of partitions of $n$ into $d$-th powers, defined by

$$
\prod_{k=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{1-q^{k^d}}=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}p_d(n)q^n.
$$

A sequence of positive real numbers $(a_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ is log-concave when $a_n^2\geq a_{n-1}a_{n+1}$ for $n\geq 1$. **Strengthened log-concavity conjecture.** There is an integer $M_d$ such that, for all $n\geq M_d$,

$$
p_d(n)^2\geq p_d(n-1)p_d(n+1)\left(1+\frac{1}{n^d}\right).
$$

In particular, $(p_d(n))_{n\geq M_d}$ is log-concave. This strengthens eventual log-concavity by prescribing an explicit multiplicative margin. The source supplies the formulation and computational motivation but no proof or resolution.
record.source_name: Maciej Ulas, “Some observations and speculations on partitions into d-th powers”, arXiv:2102.05355 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.05355

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2021).

record.title: Noncanonical dual-graph conjecture for generalized snake order polytopes
record.statement: Let $Q_{\mathbf{w}}$ be a poset with Jordan--Hölder poset $J(Q_{\mathbf{w}})=\widehat{P}(\mathbf{w})$, and let a **turn** mean the specified local turn in the generalized snake poset. A regular triangulation has a dual graph whose vertices are maximal simplices and whose edges join simplices sharing a facet. **Noncanonical dual-graph conjecture.** If $J(Q_{\mathbf{w}})=\widehat{P}(\mathbf{w})$ contains a turn, then $\mathcal{O}(Q_{\mathbf{w}})$ has a regular triangulation whose dual graph is not isomorphic to the dual graph of the canonical triangulation. The claim is supported by computations, while the ladder case has the same dual graph for every triangulation.
record.source_name: Matias von Bell, Benjamin Braun, Derek Hanely, Khrystyna Serhiyenko, Julianne Vega, Andrés R. Vindas-Meléndez and Martha Yip, “Triangulations, order polytopes, and generalized snake posets”, arXiv:2102.11306 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.11306

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2021).

record.title: Nonexistence conjecture for even-order deeply critical oriented cliques
record.statement:
Let $n$ be the order of a deeply critical oriented clique, meaning an oriented graph $\overrightarrow{G}$ that is an absolute oriented clique and satisfies

$$
\chi_o(\overrightarrow{G}-xy)=\chi_o(\overrightarrow{G})-2
$$

for every arc $xy$ of $\A(\overrightarrow{G})$. **Even-order nonexistence conjecture.** There are no deeply critical oriented cliques of even order. The paper presents this as an open problem motivated by the lack of even-order examples despite intensive computer search; it does not provide a proof or disproof.
record.source_name: Christopher Duffy, Pavan P D, Sandeep R. B. and Sagnik Sen, “On Deeply Critical Oriented Cliques”, arXiv:2103.17140 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.17140

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2021).

record.title: The computational discrete entropoid root hardness conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\mathbb{E}_{p^2}$ be an entropoid, with $p=2q+1$ a safe prime having $\lambda$ bits, and let $g$ generate $\mathbb{E}^*_{(p-1)^2}$. Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an algorithm for CDERP. The **CDERP hardness conjecture.** Over uniformly chosen $(\mathbf{B},\mathfrak{b})\xleftarrow{\mathbf{r}}\mathbb{L}$, the probability that

$$
\mathcal{A}\left(x^{(\mathbf{B},\mathfrak{b})},(\mathbf{B},\mathfrak{b})\right)=x
$$

is $\mathtt{negl}(\lambda)$. This conjectures the computational difficulty of extracting non-associative entropoid roots; the paper gives no proof or resolution.
record.source_name: Danilo Gligoroski, “Entropoid Based Cryptography”, arXiv:2104.05598 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.05598

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2021).

record.title: Non-APN and non-permutation conjecture for the family $C_u$
record.statement:
Let $m>3$ and let $uein \mathbb{F}_{2^m}$. Define

$$
\phi_u\colon (\mathbb{F}_{2^m})^3\to \mathbb{F}_{2^m},\qquad \phi_u(x,y,z)=x^3+uy^2z,
$$

and

$$
C_u(x,y,z)=\bigl(\phi_u(x,y,z),\phi_u(y,z,x),\phi_u(z,x,y)\bigr).
$$

**Non-APN and non-permutation conjecture.** The function $C_u$ is not APN. Further, if $u\neq 0$, then $C_u$ is not a permutation.

The case $m=3$ is exceptional, since the family contains APN permutations there. The authors report computational evidence that the conjectured non-permutation statement holds for several odd dimensions, while the APN question remains open for all $m>3$.
record.source_name: Christof Beierle, Claude Carlet, Gregor Leander and Léo Perrin, “A Further Study of Quadratic APN Permutations in Dimension Nine”, arXiv:2104.08008 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.08008

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2021).

record.title: Jet graphs of very well covered graphs are very well covered
record.statement: Let $G$ be a very well covered graph, and for $s\in\mathbb{N}$ let $\mathcal{J}_s(G)$ denote its $s$-th jet graph. A graph is **very well covered** if all its minimal vertex covers have the same cardinality and this cardinality is half the number of vertices. **Jet-graph conjecture.** For every $s\in\mathbb{N}$, the graph $\mathcal{J}_s(G)$ is very well covered. The conjecture is motivated by the fact that jets of the complete bipartite graphs $K_{n,n}$ are very well covered, and computational evidence shows that the jets up to third order of Favaron's example of a very well covered graph have the same property; the general case remains open.
record.source_name: Federico Galetto, Elisabeth Helmick and Molly Walsh, “Jet Graphs”, arXiv:2104.08933 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.08933

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2021).

record.title: The exceptional-graph conjecture for average color degree and rainbow matchings
record.statement:
Let $G$ be an edge-colored graph, let $\hat d(G)$ be its average color degree, and let $\widetilde{K_4}$ denote the exceptional edge-colored graph referred to in the source. A **rainbow matching** is a matching whose edges have pairwise distinct colors. **Exceptional-graph conjecture.** If $\hat d(G)\geq 2k-1$, then, unless $G$ is $\widetilde{K_4}$, the graph $G$ contains a rainbow matching of size at least $k$.

The authors state this as an affirmative expected answer to a question they were unable to resolve for all graphs. The precise definition of $\widetilde{K_4}$ is not included in the supplied context, so the exceptional case should be checked against the paper.
record.source_name: Wenling Zhou, “Large rainbow matchings in edge-colored graphs with given average color degree”, arXiv:2105.10632 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.10632

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2021).

record.title: Facial edge-coloring conjecture for plane graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a plane graph, and let $
u$ be a positive integer. An **$
u$-facial edge-coloring** of $G$ is an edge-coloring in which all edges on every facial trail of length at most $
u+1$ receive distinct colors. **Facial edge-coloring conjecture.** Every plane graph admits an $
u$-facial edge-coloring with at most

$$
3
u+1
$$

colors for every $
u\geq 1$. This conjecture is known for $
u\leq 3$: the cases $
u\leq 2$ were previously confirmed, and the paper proves the case $
u=3$; the general case remains open.
record.source_name: Mirko Horňák, Borut Lužar and Kenny Štorgel, “3-facial edge-coloring of plane graphs”, arXiv:2105.14856 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.14856

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2021).

record.title: Hurwitz stability conjecture for the peak polynomial sequence
record.statement:
Let $M_{n,r}(x)$ and $\widetilde{M}_{n,r}(x)$ be the polynomial sequences defined by the preceding peak-polynomial recurrences, and define $T_{n,r}(x)$ by

$$
(1+x)T_{n,r}(x)=xM_{n,r}(x^2)+\widetilde{M}_{n,r}(x^2).
$$

**Hurwitz stability conjecture.** The polynomial $T_{n,r}(x)$ is Hurwitz stable for all $r\ge 2$ and $n\in\mathbb{N}$. The sequence is introduced after Hurwitz stability has been established for the associated peak-polynomial sequences and their Turán expressions. The conjecture is based on empirical evidence and computer arithmetic, and its resolution is not specified in the source.
record.source_name: Ming-Jian Ding and Bao-Xuan Zhu, “Stability of combinatorial polynomials and its applications”, arXiv:2106.12176 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.12176

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2021).

record.title: Optimal construction conjecture for the partially directed k-triangle Turán problem
record.statement:
For $k\geq 2$, let $\vec T_k$ be the partially directed $k$-triangle, and let $\pi(\vec T_k,\theta)$ denote the weighted Turán density in which directed edges have weight $\theta$.

**Optimal construction conjecture.**

$$
\pi\left(\vec T_k,(1-1/k)^{-k+1}\right)=1
$$

for every $k\geq 2$.

The conjecture asserts that the construction obtained by partitioning the vertices into parts of sizes approximately $n/k$ and $(k-1)n/k$, then directing the relevant edges toward the first part, is optimal. The source says it is confirmed for $k=2$; the general case remains open.
record.source_name: Dingding Dong, Nitya Mani and Yufei Zhao, “Enumerating k-SAT functions”, arXiv:2107.09233 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.09233

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2021).

record.title: The Blaschke–Santaló bounds for the Steklov–Neumann functional
record.statement:
Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ be a bounded, convex, open set, and let $F(\Omega)$ denote the functional introduced in the paper.

**Blaschke–Santaló bounds.** For every such $\Omega$,

$$
1\leq F(\Omega)\leq 2.
$$

These bounds would describe the conjectured range of the functional for convex planar domains; the paper presents numerical evidence for them, with collapsing rectangles asymptotically approaching the lower value and collapsing triangles asymptotically approaching the upper value.
record.source_name: Antoine Henrot and Marco Michetti, “A comparison between Neumann and Steklov eigenvalues”, arXiv:2107.10075 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.10075

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of July 2021).

record.title: The toughness condition for connected {2,4}-factors
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph of order at least three, and write $\omega(G\setminus S)$ for the number of components of $G\setminus S$. A connected $\\{2,4\\}$-factor is a connected spanning subgraph whose vertex degrees all belong to $\\{2,4\\}$. **The connected $\\{2,4\\}$-factor conjecture.** If

$$
\omega(G\setminus S)\leq \frac{1}{2}|S|+1
$$

for every $S\subseteq V(G)$, then $G$ admits a connected $\\{2,4\\}$-factor. The source states that this would simplify the preceding theorem, notes that it is true for strongly $2$-tough graphs, and gives a restricted case in which it can be confirmed.
record.source_name: Morteza Hasanvand, “Spanning tree-connected subgraphs with small degrees”, arXiv:2205.05044 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.05044

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2022).

record.title: Genericity conjecture for dope matrices
record.statement:
Let $P\in\mathbb{C}[x]$ be a polynomial, let $\Lambda=(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_m)$ be an $m$-tuple of distinct complex numbers, and let $D_P(\Lambda)$ denote the associated $m\times(n+1)$ dope matrix. For generic $\Lambda$, write $\mathcal{D}_n^{\operatorname{gen}(m)}$ for the set of such matrices.

**Genericity conjecture.** For $m\geq 3$, $\mathcal{D}_n^{\operatorname{gen}(m)}$ consists exactly of the $m\times(n+1)$ $\{0,1\}$-matrices such that, for every $k\in[0,n]$, there are at most $k$ nonzero entries in the last $k+1$ columns.

The condition is known to be sufficient when $m=1$ and, by the paper's theorem, when $m=2$. Computations for $m=3$ and $n\leq 6$ support the conjecture, but the general case $m\geq 3$ remains open.
record.source_name: Noga Alon, Noah Kravitz and Kevin O'Bryant, “Counting Dope Matrices”, arXiv:2205.09302 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.09302

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2022).

record.title: Rooted $(3+1)$-free $e$-positivity conjecture
record.statement:
Let $(P,\leq_P)$ be a poset, let $G(P)$ be its incomparability graph, and let $G(P)_*^r$ denote this graph rooted at $r\in P$. Let $X_0(G(P)_*^r)$ be the rooted chromatic symmetric function, and call it **$e$-positive** when each coefficient in its expansion as a polynomial in the root variable has an $e$-positive symmetric-function coefficient.

**Rooted $(3+1)$-free $e$-positivity conjecture.** For every $r\in P$, if $P-r$ is $(\mathbf{3}+\mathbf{1})$-free, then

$$
X_0(G(P)_*^r)
$$

is $e$-positive.

The authors report computer verification for posets with at most $8$ vertices, but the general assertion remains open.
record.source_name: Nicholas A. Loehr and Gregory S. Warrington, “A rooted variant of Stanley's chromatic symmetric function”, arXiv:2206.05392 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.05392

Status: **open** according to the source (as of June 2022). “The influential paper contains an open problem that we call Stanley's Chromatic Conjecture for Trees:”

record.title: The regularity conjecture for powers of edge ideals of gap-free graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a gap-free graph and let $I=I(G)$ be its edge ideal. For each integer $s\ge 2$, write $I^{(s)}$ for the $s$-th symbolic power of $I$. **Regularity conjecture.** One has

$$
\operatorname{reg}(I^s)=\operatorname{reg}(I^{(s)})=\max\{\operatorname{reg} I+s-1,2s\}.
$$

The proposed formula extends the preceding results for small powers, which establish the equality for $s\le 3$ and prove the displayed bound for $s=2,3$ in the gap-free case. Whether the formula holds for every $s\ge 2$ is left open in the source.
record.source_name: Nguyen Cong Minh and Thanh Vu, “Characterization of graphs whose a small power of their edge ideals has a linear free resolution”, arXiv:2208.13745 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.13745

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2022).

record.title: The μ-PageRank monotonicity and range conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $[?]$-PageRank be the PageRank vector $[?]$ of $G$, and write $[?](i)$ for the value at node $i$. For $[?]>0$, let $[?]$ denote an increment of the parameter.

**μ-PageRank monotonicity and range conjecture.** The function $([?])_i$ is monotonic for all $i$ and

$$
\max_i\pi_\mu(i)-\min_i\pi_\mu(i)\leq\max_i\pi_{\mu+\alpha}(i)-\min_i\pi_{\mu+\alpha}(i)
$$

for all $[?]>0$.

This is the formal version of the two preceding empirical claims. The source motivates it with numerical experiments, but gives no proof or resolution.
record.source_name: Cory Glover, Tyler Jones, Mark Kempton and Alice Oveson, “Effects of Backtracking on PageRank”, arXiv:2211.13353 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.13353

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2022).

record.title: Pointwise convergence conjecture for hook-length mass functions
record.statement:
For $t \geq 4$, let $f_{t;n}(x)$ be the scaled mass function associated with the distribution of $\hat{Y}_t(n)$, and let $g_t(x)$ be the corresponding limiting function. **Pointwise convergence conjecture.** For all $x>0$,

$$
f_{t;n}(x)\to g_t(x)\qquad\text{as }n\to\infty.
$$

The conjecture asks whether the scaled probability mass functions converge pointwise in the regime $t\geq 4$. Convergence of the cumulative distribution functions to a shifted Gamma distribution is known, while the corresponding pointwise convergence of the mass functions had not been studied; numerical evidence supports the claim.
record.source_name: Hannah Lang, Hamilton Wan and Nancy Xu, “Distributions of Hook Lengths Divisible by Two or Three”, arXiv:2207.06486 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.06486

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2022).

record.title: The Möbius-function conjecture for signed Wachs permutations
record.statement:
Let $n\in\mathbb{P}$, and let $\mu(u,v)$ denote the Möbius function of the Bruhat-order interval $[u,v]$ in the poset of signed Wachs permutations $\operatorname{\mathcal{W}}(B_n)$. **Möbius-function conjecture.** For all $u,v\in\operatorname{\mathcal{W}}(B_n)$,

$$
\mu(u,v)\in\{0,1,-1\}.
$$

The authors verified the conjecture for $n\leqslant 6$. They also note that the corresponding statement for ordinary Wachs permutations follows from this one through the stated poset interval isomorphism.
record.source_name: Francesco Brenti and Paolo Sentinelli, “Wachs permutations, Bruhat order and weak order”, arXiv:2212.04932 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.04932

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2022).
